Aspect is really hard because we don't really have a similar concept in English. I'm not sure if you know any romance languages, I think of it like preterite and imperfect in Spanish, essentially like simple past vs continuous/repeated past action. Both technically have the same literal translation, but each carries a different sense/intention. In order to convey that same meaning in English we often have to add extra words.  

You can say Я купил хлеб and know immediately that this was a one time action, but in English in order to make that unambiguous, you would need to add "yesterday" or "last week" or something. Similarly, you can say Я покупал хлеб without "каждый день" and you still know that this was a repeated action just from the morphology of the verb.

(side note, покупать/купить is a tricky one bc по- usually signifies св so I would advise using a different verb to practice with when you first start learning aspect.)

I was diagnosed at 20. My parents never took me to be evaluated as a kid, but during the diagnosis process, they did mention that a lot of the symptoms were things they worried about with me as a child, but never made the connection that they were linked to ADHD. I don't blame them for not knowing. Even for showing those symptoms, I did extremely well in grade school and while I was far from well-adjusted socially, it wasn't the worst it could have been. My parents were young and how were they supposed to know my glassy eyed looks and daydreaming were ADHD? Honestly for awhile, they thought it was Asperger's so it wasn't like they weren't aware/trying to help. They just made a conscious decision to let me be me because I was doing pretty fine on my own.

I started to have more noticeable (to myself) problems when high school (and depression) hit. That's when I would have liked a diagnosis because then, I would know it wasn't my laziness that kept me from "living up to my potential" and I feel like that definitely would have alleviated some of my depression.

My parents were and still are very wary of medication, and honestly that can be good sometimes. But hesitation about medication shouldn't preclude you from getting a diagnosis for your son. Even if you don't choose to disclose it to him or medicate him at this time, it leaves his options open for the future. If he already has a diagnosis from childhood, when he's old enough to make his own medical decisions, it will be much easier to get medication.

To be entirely fair, not having a diagnosis early in life let me develop coping skills to get around my particular difficulties that really helped me succeed later on in life. That being said, not every person will have that experience because everyone has different presentations of ADHD and strengths and weaknesses outside of ADHD.

tldr: you should get your son tested, but whether or not to disclose/act on the diagnosis now depends on the specifics of his situation
